The fault is concentrated in [src/user/email.js](/app/src/user/email.js:47). The per-user pending marker expires after `emailConfirmInterval` minutes, while the confirmation record expires after a hard-coded day. That lets an old link remain valid after pending state disappears. The email-specific pending check can also return `null` instead of a strict `false`.

The fix should add `getValidationExpiry(uid)` using the store’s live millisecond TTL, add `canSendValidation(uid, email)` with an awaited pending check and the specified `ttlMs + intervalMs < expiryMs` rule, and make explicit expiry clear both keys. `sendValidationEmail` should use the configured expiry in days for the confirmation lifetime.

Existing tests cover sending and confirmation, but not TTL bounds or resend timing. **Uncertainty:** `emailConfirmExpiry` is absent from the current defaults and settings template, so its configuration source needs to be established. I made no project source or test changes because this role is restricted to fault localization.

Updated email confirmation handling in [src/user/email.js](/app/src/user/email.js). Pending checks now return strict booleans, the new TTL and resend helpers use the store’s live millisecond TTL, and both confirmation keys use the configured expiry. Explicit expiry clears both keys, and orphaned codes are rejected. I also added a one day default, an admin setting, and regression tests.

Verification: ESLint and diff checks passed; the full user suite passed 256 tests, followed by 7 focused confirmation tests and 6 email API tests.

VERDICT: FIX

The patch has two correctness issues in [src/user/email.js](/app/src/user/email.js):

- At line 58, `isValidationPending(uid, '')` treats the supplied empty email as though no email was supplied and can return `true` for a different pending address. Check whether the argument was supplied before comparing addresses.
- At line 75, `canSendValidation(uid, email)` checks whether the *requested email* matches the pending one. Requesting a different address therefore bypasses the configured resend interval and replaces the active confirmation. Base resend eligibility on whether the user has any pending confirmation.
